label: b35: DQN local cell (snek3 defaults: PER, fork 4, shield, eval epsilon), hist8 at 3M steps, seed 8 of 8
notes: Batch b35: row A1 of the algorithm series (plans/algoExploration/a-return-tail.md), DQN as the control for every value-based row, on the 26+16 observation (hist8) and b27's reward (preset b2, step penalty 0.01, win 100). Two cells of four seeds. paper (b35a-d): the Munchausen paper's DQN-Adam plumbing -- Adam 5e-5 eps 3.125e-4, batch 32, one gradient step per 4 moves (replay ratio 0.25), 1M uniform replay with a 20k prefill, hard target copy every 2,000 updates (8,000 moves), 1-step, epsilon linear 1.0 -> 0.01 over 250k moves then held, no shield, no fork, one lane; 10M moves = 10M counted steps, eval every 2,500 steps. local (b35e-h): snek3's own DQN defaults -- lr 1e-5, batch 128, replay ratio 1, 100k PER 0.6, target every 8 updates, the eval-driven epsilon 0.4 -> 0.002 with the shield 0.8 and the 4-branch fork; 3M counted steps = 12M moves (b2's cap), eval every 1,000. Both cells sized under 8 h with stage B and the hof passes from the laptop's measured 1,865 st/s (paper) and 357 st/s (local). Read against PPO's hist8 table (b27q-x) and each other: the gap between the cells is what the fork, the shield, PER and the fast target are worth on this game. Prediction (agent, 2026-09-17): the local cell reaches 90% perfect by 1M counted steps as b2 did and shows a stage-B density in the 40-60% range, well under PPO's 94-95%; the paper cell learns more slowly (epsilon is 0.5 for the first 125k moves), reaches a perfect rate above zero by 3M moves and ends below the local cell on density, because uniform replay and an unshielded epsilon 0.01 keep feeding endgame deaths the fork was built to avoid. Pinned to the desktop, one wave.
